subject: GPU burst containment & staged recovery commitments
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Suresh Rao <suresh@luminix.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: GPU burst containment & staged recovery commitments

Hi Suresh,

We detected a sharp burst of GPU-backed requests against your dedicated pool starting 09:05 PDT that caused headroom to drop below our soft threshold and triggered throttling for ~22 minutes. Immediate actions taken:

- Shifted a portion of Luminix traffic to a warm standby pool to reduce pressure.
- Engaged emergency throttling at the gateway to protect latency SLOs for other tenants.
- Restarted the autoscaler coordinator to clear a stuck scale-up token and applied a temporary override to allow one immediate scale-up.

Current status: Traffic is steady and we've observed a ~70% reduction in error rate; the queue depth is returning to normal. We expect full behavioral normalization within 60 minutes, with a follow-up update in 45 minutes.

What we're doing next (short-term):
- Karthik's team is investigating root cause; we'll provide an interim technical note within 3 business hours.
- We'll propose a remediation and compensation package if we confirm customer-impacting degradation.

Attached: initial-incident-timeline.pdf (incident timeline and raw graphs).

Ticket: RED-9123

If you are seeing any specific traces or request ids, paste them back and we'll prioritize them.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-21T14:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: GPU burst containment & staged recovery commitments — preliminary root cause & next steps

Hi all,

Preliminary findings (interim, under investigation):

- Trigger: Luminix's recurring batch hit a new code path that sends many long-context requests that bypass our prefix cache (high token counts + variable prefix patterns).
- Effect: The continuous batcher attempted to pack large variable-length inputs into GPU batches, causing excessive KV memory churn. That churn elevated device memory pressure and led to intermittent OOMs on some devices while the autoscaler did not respond fast enough due to a gating check introduced in last month's scale policy (cooldown gating + one-node-per-minute rate limit).
- Secondary factor: A small race in the autoscaler ledger could leave a 'scale token' in limbo if coordinator restart coincided with scale decision; this prevented the scheduler from accepting the first queued scale-up in a narrow window.

Immediate remediation (implemented):
- Reverted the recent packer heuristic change to avoid packing extreme variable-length inputs into single large batches.
- Reduced autoscaler cooldown from 180s -> 60s for dedicated pools and increased the scale-up rate cap for emergency overrides.
- Enabled a temporary pre-warm reservation for Luminix's pool for 2 hours to absorb retry storms.

Next steps (72h plan):
- Full RCA doc with timeline, root-cause engineering notes, and a regression test will be delivered in 72 hours.
- Longer-term changes: add KV-cache pressure metrics to dashboards, add e2e CI for packing heuristics, and harden autoscaler ledger consistency with a small consensus-style ack.
- Customer-facing remediation: coordinate with CS on credit and a follow-up technical review session.

I'm attaching the draft of the root cause write-up: runcause-draft.md. Expect an internal postmortem to be published after we validate the timeline.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Serving Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
